items.title: Brasilianista progressista, amigo de Hobsbawm, lembra como perdeu apoio do PT

items.summary: [RESUMO] O britânico Leslie Bethell, um dos mais importantes pesquisadores da história do Brasil, completa 90 anos em fevereiro. Morador do Rio há quase duas décadas, ele relembra sua origem operária, a formação intelectual e os vínculos com o Brasil, onde vive o paradoxo de se definir como uma pessoa de esquerda, mas ser visto como um historiador conservador, defensor do Império Britânico. Bethell mostrou nos anos 1970 como a intervenção da Marinha inglesa foi crucial para pôr fim ao tráfico de escravizados, depois coordenou a prestigiosa coleção de história da América Latina de Cambridge e fundou, nos anos 1990, o Centro de Estudos Brasileiros na Universidade de Oxford, extinto em 2007 por desinteresse do governo brasileiro e de seus pares acadêmicos ingleses. items.title: New elementary school enrollment to drop below 300,000 for 1st time amid low birth rate

items.summary: The number of children entering elementary schools in Korea is expected to fall below 300,000 for the first time next year amid the country's low birth rate, data showed Sunday. The number of first graders, born in 2020, entering elementary school for the 2027 academic year, is expected to fall short of 300,000, just three years after dropping below the 400,000 mark, according to data compiled by the Korean Statistical Information Service (KOSIS) and the Korean Educational Development Institute (KEDI). The decline comes as only 272,337 babies were born in 2020, down 10 percent from a year earlier, according to the Ministry of Data and Statistics. A total of 301,442 students enrolled as elementary school freshmen this year, barely surpassing the 300,000 mark and marking the lowest level since 1964, when the ministry began compiling related data. The figure is expected to fall further next year to roughly one-fourth of the 1.05 million recorded in 1968. The plan was discussed in a recent meeting with importers of foreign-produced bottled water, according to the officials from the environment ministry. The meeting was a routine consultation with industry officials, and the ministry is still undecided on whether to apply the mandate to offshore brands, they added. Korea has required all bottled water produced and sold domestically to be label-free starting early this year, replacing physical labels with QR codes on bottle caps and external packaging. The mandate is expected to reduce the country's annual plastic usage by 2,270 metric tons, according to the ministry of climate, energy and environment. Bottled water produced overseas, however, is excluded from the mandate and is sold with traditional labels. items.title: GCC states to sign landmark railway agreement in Bahrain on Sunday
items.title_zh: 海湾合作委员会宣布将于周日在巴林签署具有里程碑意义的铁路协议
items.summary: MANAMA — Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) member states are set to sign a general agreement on the GCC railway project on Sunday in Bahrain's capital, Manama, marking a major step toward connecting the six Gulf countries through an integrated rail network.The signing ceremony will be held under the patronage and in the presence of Bahrain's Crown Prince and Prime Minister Prince Salman bin Hamad Al Khalifa, with the participation of GCC transport ministers and the bloc's secretary-general.The GCC General Secretariat outlined four key pillars of the agreement, covering project implementation, technical integration, coordination and regional connectivity.Under the first pillar, member states will commit to implementing and operating the railway project in accordance with an agreed action plan and timeline.The second pillar focuses on technical and operational compatibility, ensuring that national railway networks are interconnected and comply with common specifications, interoperability requirements and safety standards.The third pillar establishes coordination and follow-up mechanisms, defining the responsibilities of member states and strengthening cooperation with the GCC Railways Authority to monitor implementation progress and address potential obstacles.The fourth pillar aims to enhance connectivity across the Gulf by providing safe, cost-effective and environmentally friendly transportation for passengers and freight.The project is also expected to facilitate trade and strengthen economic and social ties among GCC member states.

items.title: 1,205 contraband seizures recorded at Saudi Customs ports last week
items.title_zh: 上周在沙特海关港口记录了1,205起违禁品缉获
items.summary: RIYADH — Land, sea, and air customs ports across Saudi Arabia recorded 1,205 seizures of contraband last week. The seizures included 36 types of narcotics, such as hashish, cocaine, heroin, crystal meth and Captagon pills; 303 other prohibited substances; 879 tobacco and tobacco products; and 31 illegally transported currency. The seizures were part of the Zakat, Tax and Customs Authority’s (ZATCA) ongoing work to strengthen security and protect society from prohibited items. ZATCA reaffirmed its commitment to strict customs control over Saudi Arabia's imports and exports to protect society, in continuous coordination with its partner agencies.The authority urged the public to help combat smuggling and protect society and the national economy by reporting suspicious activity through the dedicated security hotline, 1910, by email at 1910@zatca.gov.sa, or via the international number, +9661910. Reports of smuggling and violations of the Unified Customs Law are handled in complete confidentiality, and a financial reward is offered for information that proves accurate.

items.title: Saudi Arabia deports 9,589 illegal residents in a week
items.title_zh: 沙特阿拉伯一周内驱逐9,589名非法居民
items.summary: RIYADH — Saudi security authorities arrested a total of 11,587 illegal residents in a week. The arrests were made in the joint inspections, carried out by the security forces in collaboration with the relevant government agencies, during the period between October 29 and November 4, the Ministry of Interior announced on Saturday. Those who were arrested include 6,043 violators of the Residency Law, 3,191 violators of the Border Security Law, and 2,353 violators of the Labor Law. A total of 9,589 illegal residents were deported while 23,193 violators were referred to their diplomatic missions to obtain travel documents and 9,139 violators were referred to complete their travel reservations. The total number of people who were arrested while trying to cross the border into the Kingdom accounted for 1,678. A total of 18 people were arrested while attempting to leave the Kingdom illegally. Some 29 people involved in giving transportation, shelter, and employment for violators were also arrested. A total of 41,106 expatriates, including 38,813 men and 2,293 women, are currently undergoing procedures to enforce legal measures for violations. The Ministry of Interior has warned that any person, who facilitates the illegal entry of individuals into the Kingdom, transports them on its territory, provides them with shelter or any other assistance or service, will be penalized with up to 15 years in prison and a fine of up to SR1 million, and that the vehicles used for transportation or houses used for giving shelter will be confiscated. The ministry urged the public to report any cases of violation by calling the number 911 in the regions of Makkah, Riyadh, and the Eastern Province and the numbers 999 and 996 in the rest of the Kingdom’s regions.

items.title: Syria says military cooperation with Saudi Arabia could evolve into mutual defense agreement
items.title_zh: 叙利亚称与沙特阿拉伯的军事合作可能演变为共同防御协议
items.summary: DAMASCUS — Syria's military cooperation with Saudi Arabia could eventually develop into a mutual defense agreement or lead to Damascus joining the Makkah Alliance, a Syrian diplomatic source told the Syrian Arab News Agency (SANA).The source said existing military agreements between the two countries focus on training, exchanging expertise and providing military consultations in support of their shared national interests.The cooperation primarily aims to train Syrian military personnel and strengthen the capabilities of the country's armed forces, the source said, adding that Saudi delegations are expected to begin coordination visits to Syria next month.The source indicated that the partnership could expand in the future to include a mutual defense agreement or Syria's accession to the Makkah Alliance, depending on the shared interests of both countries.However, the diplomatic source denied reports suggesting that Syria was preparing to deploy military forces to Yemen.The source said such claims were baseless, emphasizing that Syria's priorities in the coming period remain focused on consolidating internal security, advancing reconstruction and achieving economic recovery.The remarks follow the signing of a military cooperation agreement between the Saudi and Syrian defense ministries during Syrian President Ahmed Al-Sharaa's visit to Riyadh last week.

items.title: Saudi citizen arrested for transporting 8 border security violators in Jazan

items.summary: RIYADH — Security Regiments patrols in Al-Dair governorate in the southern Jazan region arrested a Saudi citizen for transporting eight border security violators in a vehicle he was driving.All the violators were taken into custody, and legal procedures were taken against them. The violators were referred to the competent authority, while the Saudi driver was referred to the Public Prosecution.The Ministry of Interior’s Agency for Security Regiments Affairs warned that anyone facilitating the entry of border security violators into Saudi Arabia, transporting them within the country, sheltering them, or providing any form of assistance or service faces penalties of up to 15 years in prison and a fine of up to SR1 million. Penalties also include confiscation of the vehicle used for transportation and the property used for shelter, as well as public naming.The agency emphasized that the offense is a major crime warranting detention and constitutes a breach of honor and trust. It urged the public to report violations of residency, labor, and border security regulations by calling 911 in the regions of Makkah, Madinah, Riyadh, and the Eastern Province or 999 and 996 elsewhere in Saudi Arabia. All reports will be treated confidentially, with no liability for those reporting, it added.

Moderate to heavy rain was experienced in several parts of the Jeddah governorate and a number of its affiliated centers on Saturday morning and afternoon. Light to moderate rainfall was recorded across various parts of Madinah region on Saturday morning, while cloudy skies continue to prevail, with further rainfall expected. In its weather forecast for Saturday, the National Center of Meteorology (NCM) expected moderate to heavy thunderstorms, potentially triggering torrential rains accompanied by hail and active winds stirring up dirt and dust, which could reduce horizontal visibility to near zero in parts of the regions of Makkah, Madinah, Hail, Qassim, the Northern Borders, and the northern parts of the Eastern Province, as well as in parts of Jazan, Asir, and Al-Baha. Light to moderate rainfall is expected in parts of Tabuk and Al-Jouf regions, as well as the northern parts of the Riyadh region, while fog formation cannot be ruled out in some areas. The NCM issued a warning of moderate rainfall in Tabuk and Taima, accompanied by strong winds, near-zero horizontal visibility, hail, flowing torrents, and thunderstorms. The center stated that the weather conditions are expected to continue until 8 p.m. It warned of heavy rainfall in the Hail region, accompanied by hail, active winds, and near-zero horizontal visibility. The warning covers the city of Hail, its governorates, open areas, and highways. The NCM issued a warning of moderate rainfall in the Al-Baha region, accompanied by strong winds, near-zero visibility, torrential flows, hail, and thunderstorms in the governorates of Al-Makhwah, Qalwa, Ghamid Al-Zanad, and Al-Hujrah, as well as neighboring areas. Light rainfall, accompanied by active winds, reduced horizontal visibility, and thunderstorms, is also expected in the city of Al-Baha and the governorates of Baljurashi, Al-Mandaq, Bani Hassan, the villages, and Al-Aqiq, as well as neighboring areas. The center stated that the weather conditions are expected to continue until 8 p.m.

items.title: Cruise missile and UAV, fired by Houthi militia, intercepted over Riyadh
items.title_zh: 胡塞民兵发射的巡航导弹和无人机在利雅得上空被拦截
items.summary: RIYADH — A cruise missile launched by the terrorist Houthi militia toward the Riyadh region was intercepted and destroyed. This was revealed by Maj. Gen. Turki Al-Maliki, spokesperson of the Coalition to Restore Legitimacy in Yemen. A UAV was also intercepted and destroyed in the Riyadh region, he said.

items.title: Saudi Arabia extends operational lifespan of taxis, rental cars by up to six months
items.title_zh: 沙特阿拉伯将出租车和租车的使用寿命延长至6个月
items.summary: RIYADH — The Transport General Authority (TGA) has announced an extension of up to six months to the operational lifespan of vehicles used in taxi services and private car rentals, extending the deadline to June 30, 2027. The decision applies to vehicles whose permitted operational lifespan expires at the end of 2026, allowing establishments to continue using them for an additional period. The authority explained that the extension aims to enhance operational flexibility, ensure service continuity and ease the burden of replacing vehicles, while maintaining safety requirements and service quality standards. The decision also seeks to help establishments maximize the use of their existing vehicles and improve operational efficiency. The TGA emphasized that the measure forms part of its ongoing efforts to develop the regulatory environment for transport activities, enhance service sustainability and support the sector’s long-term growth.

items.title: Muslim World League condemns Houthi attempts to target Makkah, Madinah with missiles and drones
items.title_zh: 世界穆斯林联盟谴责胡塞武装企图用导弹和无人机瞄准麦加和麦地那
items.summary: MAKKAH — The Muslim World League (MWL) has strongly condemned the Houthi militia’s continued attempts to target Muslim holy sites in Makkah and Madinah, as well as civilian areas across Saudi Arabia. In a statement issued by its General Secretariat, MWL Secretary-General and Chairman of the Organization of Muslim Scholars Sheikh Dr. Mohammed Al-Issa denounced the militia’s deliberate attacks using ballistic missiles and drones, which were successfully intercepted by Saudi air defenses, describing them as violations of the sanctity of holy sites and innocent lives. Al-Issa warned that the attacks risk provoking the sentiments of more than two billion Muslims, condemning the militia’s repeated acts of terrorism and violations of religious and humanitarian principles. He stressed that the actions of the group calling itself Ansar Allah constitute a betrayal of religion and Muslims and contradict the guidance of God and His Messenger. Speaking on behalf of the MWL’s councils, bodies and international assemblies, Al-Issa reaffirmed full solidarity with Saudi Arabia in all measures taken to deter the attackers and protect holy sites and innocent lives. He concluded by praying for the Kingdom’s continued security and the protection of its leadership and people.
